evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Not present. Rep moves straight into zip code verification and logistics probing without framing the call length, outcome promise, or waiting for customer agreement.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name: 'My name is Jean Ben'; Moving day: 'October timeframe...week of the 26 and then to actually move on the thirtieth'; Route: 'from Grandberry Texas to San antonio' with zip codes 76049 to 78259; Size: '3400' square feet (customer corrects rep's 3000 estimate).
evidence_quotes.walkthrough_branch: Rep correctly identifies 3400 sq ft as requiring virtual walkthrough: 'For a house the size, we need to gather more information and we need to do a virtual walkthrough...video call or a FaceTime so that we'll be able to...give you an on target estimate.' Customer agrees and rep schedules walkthrough at 4:00 PM same day.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moves from size confirmation directly into address and property detail collection without asking 'what are your biggest concerns about this move?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.packing_services: Not offered. Packing is mentioned only as part of the customer's stated prep timeline ('we're looking at a packing making ready the week of the 26'), never offered as a service option.

top_strength: Rep correctly identified the 3,400 sq ft move as requiring a virtual walkthrough per the script and smoothly routed the call to that process rather than attempting an on-call quote, with clear confirmation of the 4:00 PM same-day walkthrough time.
coaching_note: Section 1 is missing the critical quid pro quo framing ('10 to 15 minutes, walk away with a dependable quote') — jump straight into zip codes and probing without setting expectation or getting customer buy-in first; also Section 2's 'Their Agenda' question ('what are your biggest concerns?') should be asked before logistics detail-gathering begins, even on a walkthrough-routed call.
